headline: TREK’s MCP/browser surface creates the main risk: prompt injection and cascading errors are plausible; direct data leakage and compliance issues are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK exposes MCP and browser execution, so if Argo Workflows outputs are passed into TREK through files, APIs, or MCP, injected instructions could be interpreted. Argo itself has REST/gRPC and allowlisted egress, but no direct bridge is documented, so the interaction is inferred and uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Argo outputs are copied into TREK via MCP, file upload, or pasted text
IF TREK treats retrieved content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that ingest arbitrary text
Add a fixed instruction/data separator in TREK prompts
Require manual review of any Argo-generated content before execution
Log and flag prompt-like tokens in imported artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo touches artifacts and parameters, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets. TREK also has local files and logs, so a shared workspace or copied outputs could expose sensitive travel data. Argo’s allowlisted egress and TREK’s browser/network surfaces make leakage plausible, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem, upload directory, or copied workspace
IF Argo artifacts contain user parameters that TREK later renders or logs
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Restrict TREK log access to operators only
Redact secrets before passing artifacts between agents
Review outbound destinations in both agents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo has REST/gRPC and allowlisted egress, while TREK has browser, MCP, WebSocket, and collaborative multi-instance behavior. The profiles do not show shared write targets or overlapping mutable resources, so a direct write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because TREK’s collaboration model could still collide with external orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external resource without locking
IF TREK multi-instance sessions and Argo jobs target the same mutable record
mitigations: Assign separate output paths
Serialize writes to shared resources
Use unique job IDs and record IDs
Check for duplicate updates before commit
requires-engineering: add distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is described as a real-time collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream content as actionable. If Argo-produced artifacts or parameters are fed into TREK without verification, TREK could propagate errors into reservations, budgets, or documents. Argo’s workflow outputs and TREK’s downstream planning role make this plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF TREK consumes Argo outputs as authoritative inputs
IF no validation step checks Argo-generated artifacts before TREK acts on them
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before TREK actions
Validate schema and ranges on imported Argo outputs
Mark imported fields as untrusted in TREK
Compare outputs against a second source
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles high-risk personal data such as email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, plus local files and logs. Argo touches artifacts and parameters, so if those are combined in a shared workflow, retention or residency mismatches can arise. The profiles do not specify jurisdictions, so the compliance concern is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF shared workflows store TREK secrets or reservations alongside Argo artifacts
IF logs retain personal data longer than the operator’s policy
mitigations: Minimize logged fields in TREK
Purge temporary files after each run
Separate sensitive travel data from workflow artifacts
Review retention settings for logs and uploads
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
